title: Wrexham beat Ipswich to reach FA Cup fifth round for first time since 1997
content:
Wrexham are dreaming of a possible glamour FA Cup tie after booking their place in the fifth round for the first time in almost 30 years.

Josh Windass’ first half goal was enough to beat fellow promotion hopefuls Ipswich Town on a cold night in north Wales.

With 14 of the 16 fourth-round ties still to be played, Phil Parkinson’s men will have to wait to discover who they will face in the next round — with the draw not due to take place until Monday evening.

However, with Chelsea also through after beating Hull City 4-0, and only Manchester United of the Premier League big guns knocked out in the third round, there are plenty of potentially mouth-watering ties for Wrexham, who are yet to have a true glamour tie in the Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac era.

Wrexham did beat Nottingham Forest in the last round and followed that by edging past Ipswich in the first of two clashes between the teams at the SToK Cae Ras inside eight days.

Next week’s meeting will have Championship points at stake, which perhaps explains why Town manager Kieran McKenna made ten changes from the team who beat Derby County on their last outing.

Wrexham, in contrast, made five changes, two of which were due to injury with Matty James and Liberato Cacace facing spells on the sidelines.

In their absence, Windass, one of those changes, put Wrexham ahead on 34 minutes, when guiding in Ryan Longman’s right wing cross to take his tally of goals for the season to nine. Ipswich caused the hosts a few anxious moments of their own in the second half.

Wrexham, however, stood tall to book their place in the fifth round for the first time since the 1996-97 season, when they eventually bowed out in the quarter-finals at Chesterfield.
